notes:
1. Retrieved October 12, 2026 from eia.gov. Every number is copied as EIA published it, at EIA's rounding; nothing is estimated, interpolated, averaged or converted. A null means EIA published no value (EIA's code NA = 'Not available'); each null has a 'note' saying what EIA shows.
2. Units fields use EIA's exact published wording (for example 'Cents per Kilowatthour', not 'cents per kWh'). Prices are nominal dollars.
3. Fields added beyond the requested shape: retrieved, released, nextRelease, unitedStates, tableTitles, per-state 'note', mostRecentMonthPublished, mostRecentAnnualPublished, and previousSeasonFinalWeek.
4. Electricity: July 2026 is the latest month in the Electric Power Monthly released September 24, 2026 (next release October 23, 2026). EIA calls these preliminary estimates based on a cutoff model sample (Form EIA-861M). All 50 states and DC have residential values. yearToDate is January-July 2026 from Table 5.6.B. The HTML tables were checked against EIA's XLSX versions of the same tables; every value matches.
5. Natural gas: July 2026 is the latest month in the Natural Gas Monthly released September 30, 2026 (next release October 30, 2026). EIA describes these as total prices paid by end users, inclusive of all tax, delivery, commodity, demand and other charges; they reflect onsystem sales prices, except in Georgia, New York and Ohio, where they are based on total gas deliveries. EIA's table is titled 'Average price of natural gas sold to residential consumers, by state' (NGM Table 20); the matching data series is 'Price of Natural Gas Delivered to Residential Consumers'. The HTML series pages were checked against Table 20; every value matches.
6. Natural gas gaps: July 2026 is NA for CT, FL, KS, LA, NH, OH, WV; the 2025 annual average is NA for CT, ME, MD, NC, RI, SC. For those states, mostRecentMonthPublished and mostRecentAnnualPublished give EIA's latest published figure with its own month or year; they are not July 2026 or 2025 values and should be labelled as such if shown.
7. Natural gas seasonality: monthly residential prices are much higher in summer than the annual average (U.S.: 26.45 in July 2026 versus 15.34 for 2025), so the annual average is the steadier figure for yearly running-cost and payback calculations.
8. Heat content: 1,036 Btu per cubic foot is EIA's 2025 U.S. average heat content of natural gas delivered to consumers (annual series, release date September 30, 2026). NGM Table 25 shows the same 2025 U.S. figure and also gives state values, which differ from the national average.
9. Heating oil and propane: EIA's 2026-27 season has started. The first weekly prices (week of October 5, 2026) were released October 7, 2026; the next release is October 15, 2026. EIA collects these prices weekly from October through March and on the second Monday of each month from April through September, but publishes no monthly averages for April-September and the weekly tables show only heating-season weeks. EIA notes that the latest week's values may be revised for late submissions and corrections.
10. Heating oil and propane prices EXCLUDE taxes (EIA: 'Dollars per Gallon Excluding Taxes'), whereas EIA describes its residential natural gas prices as including all taxes and charges. The electricity tables used here do not say whether taxes are included.
11. previousSeasonFinalWeek holds the last weekly prices of the 2025-26 season (week of March 30, 2026), read from each series' EIA history page (the 'View History' links on the weekly tables); the week of October 5, 2026 value on every history page matches the weekly table.
12. Heating oil coverage: EIA publishes residential values for 21 states. The District of Columbia is in EIA's table but null (see its note: NA every week since its last published value, 4.040 for the week of October 7, 2019). Illinois also appears in EIA's residential heating oil table, but that series covers only 1990-1991, so it is left out. Propane coverage: 38 states, no DC. Regions are EIA's own (U.S. and PADD regions, named as EIA names them); these residential tables have no West Coast (PADD 5) rows.
13. Year-on-year context from EIA's U.S. history pages: residential heating oil was 6.042 for the week of October 5, 2026, versus 3.555 for the week of October 6, 2025 and 5.535 for the week of March 30, 2026. Residential propane was 2.598, versus 2.417 and 2.674 for the same weeks.
